bull_bear.body: The company's credit rating is an important factor in determining its ability to secure funding at favorable interest rates.
bull_bear.title: Non-obvious takeaways

bull_bear.body:
- Diversified real estate and infrastructure portfolio spanning warehousing, commercial office, CFS/ICD, logistics infrastructure and emerging asset classes, enhancing business resilience
- Strategically located asset base across key industrial corridors, logistics hubs, commercial districts and consumption centres, with proximity to ports, highways, rail networks and urban infrastructure
- Substantial land bank of more than 300 acres (including planned development) giving long-term embedded development potential
- Established track record of developing and monetising industrial and logistics real estate, having developed and exited approximately 4.8 million square feet of warehousing infrastructure in partnership with leading institutional investors
- Strong parentage and operational synergies as part of the Allcargo Group ecosystem, giving established customer relationships, integrated logistics expertise and multimodal capabilities
- Experienced management team with execution expertise across real estate, logistics, warehousing and infrastructure development
- Integrated infrastructure development capabilities spanning development, infrastructure management, operational execution and asset optimisation
- Customer-centric approach focused on responsive asset management and long-term tenant partnerships
bull_bear.title: Bull — competitive strengths

bull_bear.body:
- Geopolitical tension and trade fragmentation — Management explicitly names geopolitical tensions and global trade disruptions as key near-term risks. The MD&A records heightened geopolitical tensions, persistent trade fragmentation and a military conflict in the Middle East that disrupted maritime and air traffic, with a direct bearing on freight movement, shipping costs, logistics efficiency and cross-border trade flows.
- Commodity price and fuel cost volatility — Commodity price volatility is flagged as a key near-term risk, and elevated fuel prices are stated to influence operating costs and freight movement in the near term. Energy and fuel costs also rose on the back of the Middle East conflict.
- Dependence on freight, warehousing and manufacturing demand cycles — The Company positions its logistics parks, warehousing, CFS, ICD and PFT assets against trade and manufacturing activity; the same MD&A states that trade disruption, infrastructure bottlenecks and elevated logistics costs directly impact transportation and infrastructure-linked sectors, so the demand base for these assets is cyclically exposed.
- Tighter global financial conditions — The MD&A notes that emerging markets and developing economies remain exposed to commodity price volatility and tighter global financial conditions, and cites volatility across commodity and financial markets, a structural sensitivity for a capital-intensive real estate and infrastructure developer.
- Infrastructure bottlenecks and supply chain disruption — Uncertainty is described as remaining elevated amid evolving trade dynamics, infrastructure bottlenecks and geopolitical developments, all of which bear on logistics efficiency and the utility of logistics real estate.
- Geographic concentration of the asset base — The portfolio of operational warehouses, commercial office space, CFS and ICD infrastructure, development-ready projects and land reserves is concentrated in NCR, MMR, Bengaluru, Kolkata and Nagpur, so regional demand, policy or connectivity shocks in those markets affect a large share of the portfolio.
- Regulatory and approval risk on corporate restructuring — The scheme of merger of Madanahatti Logistics and Industrial Parks Private Limited with the Company remains subject to NCLT and other statutory and regulatory approvals, with approval awaited at the date of the report; the further mergers approved on May 14, 2026 are likewise subject to regulatory approvals. Timing and outcome are outside the Company's control.
- Execution risk in converting the development pipeline — Growth depends on moving projects such as the Mubarikpur PFT from planning into operating infrastructure; the Company describes strengthening its risk management and business continuity frameworks to enhance organisational resilience and operational preparedness, but no quantified risk register is disclosed in the report sections provided.

business.body: Transindia Real Estate Limited is a diversified real estate and infrastructure development company engaged in investing, developing, owning, leasing and managing logistics parks, warehousing infrastructure, commercial office spaces, Container Freight Stations (CFS), Inland Container Depots (ICD) and Private Freight Terminal (PFT). Its portfolio comprises operational warehouses, commercial office spaces, CFS and ICD infrastructure, development-ready projects and strategically located land reserves across key growth markets including the National Capital Region (NCR), Mumbai Metropolitan Region (MMR), Bengaluru, Kolkata and Nagpur. Assets serve logistics and supply chain operators, manufacturing companies, engineering businesses, chemical companies, consumer goods companies, e-commerce players, retailers and other corporate occupiers.

business.title: Competitive strengths

outlook.body:
- Broaden the platform beyond traditional logistics-led infrastructure into logistics parks, warehousing, commercial office, industrial infrastructure and emerging real estate asset classes.
- Build scalable platforms that combine stable income generation, development-led growth and strategic infrastructure investments.
- Anchor the approach in disciplined capital allocation, active asset management, prudent risk management and a long-term investment horizon.
- Strengthen recurring rental income through leasing of existing commercial assets and acquisition of leased, income-generating commercial assets in key markets.
- Run portfolio optimisation through selective asset monetisation and capital recycling to unlock value from mature assets and create capacity for future growth investments.
- Develop the strategic land reserves of more than 300 acres across Bengaluru, Kolkata, NCR, MMR and other high-growth corridors selectively, matching development intensity and asset configuration to market demand, connectivity advantages and return thresholds.
- Convert the development pipeline into operating infrastructure, with the Mubarikpur PFT moved from planning towards execution and the Bhiwandi and Dankuni opportunities being progressed to build scale in high-demand logistics markets and industrial corridors.
- Simplify the corporate structure by merging wholly owned subsidiaries into Transindia Real Estate Limited to improve governance efficiency and optimise resource allocation.
- Embed sustainability in development philosophy through environmentally conscious planning, responsible construction methodologies and efficient infrastructure systems.
outlook.title: Strategy & capital allocation

outlook.body: Transindia Real Estate Limited invests in, develops, owns, leases and manages logistics parks, warehousing infrastructure, commercial office spaces, Container Freight Stations (CFS), Inland Container Depots (ICD) and Private Freight Terminals (PFT). It states a track record of having developed and exited approximately 4.8 million square feet of warehousing infrastructure in partnership with leading institutional investors. During FY2025-26 the expansion agenda had three visible legs. First, diversification into premium commercial office through the acquisition of 36,670 sq. ft. of commercial office space at Privilon, Andheri (East), Mumbai, intended to add income-generating area and long-term capital appreciation. Second, conversion of the development pipeline into operating infrastructure through the commencement of development activity at the 52.3-acre Mubarikpur Private Freight Terminal, positioned against the Dedicated Freight Corridor and the NCR connectivity ecosystem and expected to strengthen multimodal logistics capabilities and regional trade connectivity. Third, asset productivity in the existing commercial portfolio, with 18,906 sq. ft. of office space at the Allcargo House property leased to Credila Solutions. The forward pipeline is anchored on the upcoming Bhiwandi platform, located in one of India's largest warehousing and logistics markets with connectivity to JNPT, NH3, NH4 and Mumbai International Airport, and designed for large-scale warehousing and industrial operations serving manufacturing, retail, e-commerce, FMCG and 3PL demand. The portfolio spans operational warehouses, commercial office spaces, CFS and ICD infrastructure, development-ready projects and land reserves across NCR, MMR, Bengaluru, Kolkata and Nagpur, with a strategic land bank of more than 300 acres including planned development. Structurally, the Board approved the merger of wholly owned subsidiary Madanahatti Logistics and Industrial Parks Private Limited into the Company, with NCLT approval awaited, and after the year-end approved the merger of five further wholly owned subsidiaries. No rupee capex quantum is usable from this report: both the Capital Commitments note and the segment Additions to non-current assets disclosure arrive with no printed unit and, in the segment case, with no period attributable to the figures.
outlook.title: Capex & expansion plans

outlook.body:
- India GDP growth for F.Y.2025-26 estimated at 7.6%, revised upward from the earlier estimate of 7.4%, supported by private final consumption expenditure, government support measures and lower interest rates.
- Industrial growth revised upward to 8.8%, led by manufacturing and mining, with trade, hotels, transport and communication services also growing, reflecting resilient logistics demand.
- Sustained government capital expenditure on roads, railways, ports, industrial corridors, logistics parks and multimodal connectivity; PM GatiShakti, Bharatmala, Dedicated Freight Corridors, industrial corridors and Multimodal Logistics Parks named as the enabling initiatives.
- India warehousing market recorded more than 30 million sq. ft. of leasing in H2 2025, driven by 3PL, engineering and manufacturing, and e-commerce occupiers.
- Institutional capital inflows into Indian real estate reached a record USD 14.3 billion in CY2025, up approximately 25% year-on-year, with land and development sites over 46% of the total.
- The office segment accounted for nearly 45% of institutional real estate investments during FY25-FY26.
- Gross office leasing reached approximately 83.3 million sq. ft. in 2025, the highest ever, up nearly 8%; net absorption around 57 million sq. ft. and vacancy down to approximately 15.2%, led by GCCs, technology, BFSI and flexible workspace operators.
- Warehousing demand supported by e-commerce and quick commerce growth, manufacturing expansion under the China+1 strategy, supply chain formalisation and rising 3PL demand, with Maharashtra and Gujarat emerging as major hubs.
- Listed Indian REITs collectively manage over 125 million sq. ft. of operational commercial assets, deepening liquidity and institutional participation in income-generating real estate.
- India's real estate market projected to reach nearly USD 1 trillion by 2030, per the Chairman's message.
- Global backdrop: China projected to grow 4.4% in 2026 moderating to 4.0% in 2027, the euro area 1.1% and 1.2%, and emerging markets and developing economies 3.9% and 4.2%, with investments in highways, rail, ports, industrial corridors, warehousing and multimodal logistics strengthening supply chain resilience.
- Management flags geopolitical tensions, commodity price volatility and global trade disruptions as key near-term risks to freight movement and logistics demand.
- Development pipeline: the Mubarikpur PFT project moved from planning towards execution during F.Y.26, converting pipeline into operating infrastructure.
- Bhiwandi and Dankuni opportunities are being progressed beyond projects currently under development, to build scale across high-demand logistics markets and industrial corridors.
- Strategic land reserves of more than 300 acres across Bengaluru, Kolkata, NCR, MMR and other high-growth corridors provide embedded development potential.
- No order book is disclosed; the Company describes a development pipeline and land reserves rather than a contracted order book.
outlook.title: Demand & outlook drivers

deepdive.thesis: Transindia Real Estate Limited has received a credit rating of CARE A- with a stable outlook for its long-term bank facilities, indicating a moderate level of credit risk. The company's ability to secure funding will be crucial for its growth plans. The real estate sector in India is expected to continue growing, driven by demand for residential and commercial spaces.

currentContext.expansion: Transindia Real Estate Limited invests in, develops, owns, leases and manages logistics parks, warehousing infrastructure, commercial office spaces, Container Freight Stations (CFS), Inland Container Depots (ICD) and Private Freight Terminals (PFT). It states a track record of having developed and exited approximately 4.8 million square feet of warehousing infrastructure in partnership with leading institutional investors. During FY2025-26 the expansion agenda had three visible legs. First, diversification into premium commercial office through the acquisition of 36,670 sq. ft. of commercial office space at Privilon, Andheri (East), Mumbai, intended to add income-generating area and long-term capital appreciation. Second, conversion of the development pipeline into operating infrastructure through the commencement of development activity at the 52.3-acre Mubarikpur Private Freight Terminal, positioned against the Dedicated Freight Corridor and the NCR connectivity ecosystem and expected to strengthen multimodal logistics capabilities and regional trade connectivity. Third, asset productivity in the existing commercial portfolio, with 18,906 sq. ft. of office space at the Allcargo House property leased to Credila Solutions. The forward pipeline is anchored on the upcoming Bhiwandi platform, located in one of India's largest warehousing and logistics markets with connectivity to JNPT, NH3, NH4 and Mumbai International Airport, and designed for large-scale warehousing and industrial operations serving manufacturing, retail, e-commerce, FMCG and 3PL demand. The portfolio spans operational warehouses, commercial office spaces, CFS and ICD infrastructure, development-ready projects and land reserves across NCR, MMR, Bengaluru, Kolkata and Nagpur, with a strategic land bank of more than 300 acres including planned development. Structurally, the Board approved the merger of wholly owned subsidiary Madanahatti Logistics and Industrial Parks Private Limited into the Company, with NCLT approval awaited, and after the year-end approved the merger of five further wholly owned subsidiaries. No rupee capex quantum is usable from this report: both the Capital Commitments note and the segment Additions to non-current assets disclosure arrive with no printed unit and, in the segment case, with no period attributable to the figures.

risks.note: Management explicitly names geopolitical tensions and global trade disruptions as key near-term risks. The MD&A records heightened geopolitical tensions, persistent trade fragmentation and a military conflict in the Middle East that disrupted maritime and air traffic, with a direct bearing on freight movement, shipping costs, logistics efficiency and cross-border trade flows.

risks.risk: Commodity price and fuel cost volatility
risks.note: Commodity price volatility is flagged as a key near-term risk, and elevated fuel prices are stated to influence operating costs and freight movement in the near term. Energy and fuel costs also rose on the back of the Middle East conflict.

risks.risk: Dependence on freight, warehousing and manufacturing demand cycles
risks.note: The Company positions its logistics parks, warehousing, CFS, ICD and PFT assets against trade and manufacturing activity; the same MD&A states that trade disruption, infrastructure bottlenecks and elevated logistics costs directly impact transportation and infrastructure-linked sectors, so the demand base for these assets is cyclically exposed.

The MD&A notes that emerging markets and developing economies remain exposed to commodity price volatility and tighter global financial conditions, and cites volatility across commodity and financial markets, a structural sensitivity for a capital-intensive real estate and infrastructure developer.

risks.risk: Infrastructure bottlenecks and supply chain disruption
risks.note: Uncertainty is described as remaining elevated amid evolving trade dynamics, infrastructure bottlenecks and geopolitical developments, all of which bear on logistics efficiency and the utility of logistics real estate.

risks.risk: Geographic concentration of the asset base
risks.note: The portfolio of operational warehouses, commercial office space, CFS and ICD infrastructure, development-ready projects and land reserves is concentrated in NCR, MMR, Bengaluru, Kolkata and Nagpur, so regional demand, policy or connectivity shocks in those markets affect a large share of the portfolio.

risks.risk: Regulatory and approval risk on corporate restructuring
risks.note: The scheme of merger of Madanahatti Logistics and Industrial Parks Private Limited with the Company remains subject to NCLT and other statutory and regulatory approvals, with approval awaited at the date of the report; the further mergers approved on May 14, 2026 are likewise subject to regulatory approvals. Timing and outcome are outside the Company's control.

risks.risk: Execution risk in converting the development pipeline
risks.note: Growth depends on moving projects such as the Mubarikpur PFT from planning into operating infrastructure; the Company describes strengthening its risk management and business continuity frameworks to enhance organisational resilience and operational preparedness, but no quantified risk register is disclosed in the report sections provided.

business_model.title: What they do
business_model.body: Transindia Real Estate Limited is a diversified real estate and infrastructure development company engaged in investing, developing, owning, leasing and managing logistics parks, warehousing infrastructure, commercial office spaces, Container Freight Stations (CFS), Inland Container Depots (ICD) and Private Freight Terminal (PFT). Its portfolio comprises operational warehouses, commercial office spaces, CFS and ICD infrastructure, development-ready projects and strategically located land reserves across key growth markets including the National Capital Region (NCR), Mumbai Metropolitan Region (MMR), Bengaluru, Kolkata and Nagpur. Assets serve logistics and supply chain operators, manufacturing companies, engineering businesses, chemical companies, consumer goods companies, e-commerce players, retailers and other corporate occupiers.

demand_drivers.title: Demand & outlook drivers
demand_drivers.body:
- India GDP growth for F.Y.2025-26 estimated at 7.6%, revised upward from the earlier estimate of 7.4%, supported by private final consumption expenditure, government support measures and lower interest rates.
- Industrial growth revised upward to 8.8%, led by manufacturing and mining, with trade, hotels, transport and communication services also growing, reflecting resilient logistics demand.
- Sustained government capital expenditure on roads, railways, ports, industrial corridors, logistics parks and multimodal connectivity; PM GatiShakti, Bharatmala, Dedicated Freight Corridors, industrial corridors and Multimodal Logistics Parks named as the enabling initiatives.
- India warehousing market recorded more than 30 million sq. ft. of leasing in H2 2025, driven by 3PL, engineering and manufacturing, and e-commerce occupiers.
- Institutional capital inflows into Indian real estate reached a record USD 14.3 billion in CY2025, up approximately 25% year-on-year, with land and development sites over 46% of the total.
- The office segment accounted for nearly 45% of institutional real estate investments during FY25-FY26.
- Gross office leasing reached approximately 83.3 million sq. ft. in 2025, the highest ever, up nearly 8%; net absorption around 57 million sq. ft. and vacancy down to approximately 15.2%, led by GCCs, technology, BFSI and flexible workspace operators.
- Warehousing demand supported by e-commerce and quick commerce growth, manufacturing expansion under the China+1 strategy, supply chain formalisation and rising 3PL demand, with Maharashtra and Gujarat emerging as major hubs.
- Listed Indian REITs collectively manage over 125 million sq. ft. of operational commercial assets, deepening liquidity and institutional participation in income-generating real estate.
- India's real estate market projected to reach nearly USD 1 trillion by 2030, per the Chairman's message.
- Global backdrop: China projected to grow 4.4% in 2026 moderating to 4.0% in 2027, the euro area 1.1% and 1.2%, and emerging markets and developing economies 3.9% and 4.2%, with investments in highways, rail, ports, industrial corridors, warehousing and multimodal logistics strengthening supply chain resilience.
- Management flags geopolitical tensions, commodity price volatility and global trade disruptions as key near-term risks to freight movement and logistics demand.
- Development pipeline: the Mubarikpur PFT project moved from planning towards execution during F.Y.26, converting pipeline into operating infrastructure.
- Bhiwandi and Dankuni opportunities are being progressed beyond projects currently under development, to build scale across high-demand logistics markets and industrial corridors.
- Strategic land reserves of more than 300 acres across Bengaluru, Kolkata, NCR, MMR and other high-growth corridors provide embedded development potential.
- No order book is disclosed; the Company describes a development pipeline and land reserves rather than a contracted order book.

themes.title: Real-estate up-cycle - premium housing & redevelopment
themes.need: The residential up-cycle is now presales-led with a visible margin cost. SOBHA posted its highest-ever presales at INR 3,656cr (+76% YoY, 2.34 msf at an average INR 15,655/sqft, NCR at a record INR 1,384cr) and guided FY27 presales at +30% or better - but reported EBITDA is still only ~9.7%, guided to 17-20% only by exit-Q4, and forthcoming-project marginal cash flow was cut from ~INR 86bn to INR 68.3bn on a heavier joint-development mix. SUNTECK booked INR 787cr of presales (+20%) with ZERO launches in the quarter, with aspirational-luxury (Naigaon/Kalyan) at 21% of presales 'picking up because of the lower interest rate' - the first sign the rate-elastic end is turning on demand rather than inventory release. DLF's FY26 bookings of INR20,143cr and 50mn sq ft of rental at 95% occupancy anchor the annuity leg; LODHA/GODREJPROP/PRESTIGE-tier and MMR redevelopers (RUSTOMJEE, KALPATARU, RAYMONDREL, MANINFRA, SURAJEST) ride premiumization; PHOENIXLTD/EMBDL on mixed-use.
themes.driver: SOBHA's exit-Q4 margin ramp from ~9.7% to 17-20% is the falsifiable claim (JD-heavy growth structurally lowers marginal margins); rate-elastic aspirational absorption (SUNTECK); FY27 launch-pipeline execution and festive booking momentum.
